name: Harmony Touch, the test sequence's delay
summary: Yellow in Watch a Blu-ray: the gap between the Blu-ray's Stop and TopMenu.
description: The delay half, run three times: before the first sync (the remote holding the set of 6.8, the delay 1 s), after the sync of work/touch-firmware/sets/6.9-delay (3 s), and after the sync of 6.9-delay-back (1 s again). Yellow's short press in Watch a Blu-ray runs Test Sequence: the Sony Blu-ray's Stop, a delay step, its TopMenu. The engine sends the sequence as one list and sleeps the delay step's Duration times 1000 ms between the two commands (luaworks loader/userconfigreader.lua getSequenceActions and apihandler/activity.lua fireCommandsList, read, never seen on a unit). Yellow holds a long press, the Blu-ray's own Yellow, so the tap has to be short: the sequence goes on release, and a press held past about 0.6 s sends the Blu-ray's Yellow instead; repeat the step and note it. Predicted: the Stop's frames, then nothing, then the TopMenu's frames. From the start of the Stop to the start of the TopMenu about 1.0 to 1.4 s with the delay at 1 s, and about 3.0 to 3.4 s at 3 s; the silence before the TopMenu's first frame, which the monitor prints, about 0.8 to 1.2 s and 2.8 to 3.2 s. The decisive figure is the difference between the runs, 2000 ms with a few tens either way, since the Stop's length and the engine's overhead are the same in all three. A gap near 1 s after the 6.9-delay sync means the change was not taken; a gap near 3 s after 6.9-delay-back means the put back was not. The bench configurations hold no Sony Blu-ray, so the frames may arrive unnamed or with the catalogue's candidates: read the times from the frame log. The Flirc runs 4.10.7.
